title: spec: `supportsPause`'s TSDoc says "a declaration no execution path reads" — false as of PR #6746, which made the engine enforce it
body:
Filed by the services-lane PM (`session_01USNUyHEr7uaU6MoEWXitei`) out of **#6667 / PR #6746**, whose dispatch forbade touching `packages/spec` (contract surfaces have one owner). Unassigned, for the spec seat. Comment-only; no schema, baseline, or registry consequence.

## The stale claim

`packages/spec/src/automation/node-executor.zod.ts:288-296` documents `supportsPause` as:

> A declaration, not an enforced fact (#5703). No execution path reads it…

PR #6746 (#6667) makes that false: `AutomationEngine.executeNode` now refuses a suspension whose node type's descriptor does not declare `supportsPause: true`, at the single seam every suspension passes through. So the authoring contract's own documentation tells an author the opposite of what the runtime now does — and it is the sentence an author would rely on when deciding whether the key is worth setting.

The engine-side and CI-side copies of the same stale claim were corrected inside PR #6746 (`warnIfResumeAuthorityUndeclared`'s docblock and `scripts/check-resume-authority-declared.mjs`'s header note + both output strings). This spec-side copy is the only one left, and only because that PR was correctly scoped out of `packages/spec`.

## What the corrected text has to say

Not merely "it is enforced now" — the boundary matters, and #6746 drew it deliberately:

- a descriptor declaring `supportsPause: false` (or omitting it — the schema default) whose executor returns `suspend: true` ⇒ **the suspension is refused**, guard-class, un-routable by a `fault` edge;
- the inverse (`supportsPause: true`, never suspends) is **legal** — a capability, not an obligation;
- an executor publishing **no descriptor at all** declares nothing to enforce; its pauses stay governed by #5561's resume gate.

## Timing

Becomes false on PR #6746's merge (it is in the merge queue as of filing). `Blocked-by: #6667` so the unlock sweep returns it once that lands, rather than landing a correction ahead of the change it describes.

⚠️ **Serialization**: same file as the `isAsync` retirement card (#6748) — this one is a comment edit and should land first, with the retirement rebasing on top; or fold the two if the spec seat takes both together.

Blocked-by: #6667
